validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, well-documented, correctly classified. This row is the first of three certificated construction phases of Transco's Hillabee Expansion Project (FERC Docket CP15-16), an interstate transmission loop expansion in Alabama built to deliver gas from Transco's Station 85 pooling point in Choctaw County to a new interconnect with Sabal Trail Transmission in Tallapoosa County. Independent confirmation across four distinct origins: (1) Pipeline & Gas Journal 'First Phase of Hillabee Expansion Completed' (Jul 2017) -- 818,410 Dth/d capacity add, ~20 miles of looping, Choctaw County compressor, in-service 2017; (2) Oil & Gas Journal 'Construction nears for Hillabee expansion project' -- Choctaw County to Tallapoosa County route, May 2017 target in-service, construction starting ~2016; (3) NS Energy Business project page (nsenergybusiness.com/projects/hillabee-expansion-project) -- segment-level loop breakdown (Proctor Creek 8.52km, Hissop 4.18km, Alexander City 12km, Billingsley 7.56km = 32.26km total new pipe), diameters (42in x3, 48in x1), counties (Choctaw, Coosa, Tallapoosa, Autauga, Chilton); (4) Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Co LLC's own SEC Form 10-Q for Q2 2017 (sec.gov, filed by the regulated entity, not a press release) -- 'Hillabee Phase I increased capacity by 818 Mdth/d,' remainder placed in service July 11, 2017 (an earlier portion June 14, 2017). None of these are GEM-derived, none are abarrelfull/theodora, none cite each other. Status=operating, Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission all confirmed by context (an in-service interstate gas transmission loop). StartYear1=2017 confirmed exactly (in-service June/July 2017). Capacity=818.00 MMcf/d confirmed near-exactly by two independent numeric restatements (PGJ: 818,410 Dth/d; SEC 10-Q: 818 Mdth/d) -- Dth and Mcf are functionally equivalent units for pipeline gas capacity, so this is a strong match, not just a plausible one. The existing sheet ref (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php, a navigation page) is live but never names this specific phase and doesn't state 818 verbatim -- it should be supplemented (not deleted; it's live) with the sources below. DUPLICATE CHECK: NOT a duplicate of another roster row. Roster row P2544 (Transcontinental Gas Pipeline, Alabama, len=17.7, dia=42, cap=206.00) is very likely Hillabee Expansion Project PHASE 2 (the archived Business Wire Williams release on Phase II states capacity add of 206,660 Dth/d and ~11 miles of new pipe -- matches P2544's cap almost exactly) -- see cross_row_leads. P2733 (Phase 1) and P2544 (Phase 2) are legitimately distinct construction phases of the same certificated project with different mileage/diameter/in-service dates; keeping them as separate GEM rows is correct segment/phase-level granularity, not a double-count.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC discrepancy on Length. Two independent sources converge on a shorter figure than the sheet's 35.41 km: (1) Pipeline & Gas Journal states phase 1 built 'approximately 20 miles of pipeline looping' = 32.2 km; (2) NS Energy Business's segment-level breakdown of the four phase-1 loops (Proctor Creek 8.52 km + Hissop 4.18 km + Alexander City 12 km + Billingsley 7.56 km) sums to 32.26 km -- independently landing on almost the identical figure via a completely different method (naming the actual loop segments vs. a rounded press estimate). That is a real, non-coincidental agreement between two independent origins, and it disagrees with the sheet's 35.41 km by about 3.15 km (~9%). I could not reach the underlying FERC certificate order itself (154 FERC P 61,080 / CP15-16) to get an authoritative mileage table -- the Corps of Engineers mirror of it (saj.usace.army.mil) 403'd to scripted access, and I did not find it on elibrary.ferc.gov or ferc.gov in the time available. This is not large enough to be an existence or classification problem (the pipe unambiguously exists and is Transco/Hillabee), but it's a specific enough disagreement between two non-reprinted origins that I'm flagging it rather than silently passing 35.41 km. Not proposing a replacement number since neither of my two sources individually claims to be exhaustive/precise (one is a rounded press estimate, one is a secondary project database's segment list that could omit a short unnamed tie-in) -- a primary FERC/EIS mileage table would resolve this.

FuelSource (per gem_schema.md) means the named upstream field/plant feeding the line, not the commodity. Transco is a long-haul interstate mainline that aggregates gas from many producing basins along its length (Gulf Coast, Marcellus/Utica via laterals, etc.) rather than one dedicated origin field; the Hillabee loops themselves are capacity/compression additions on the existing mainline, not a new lateral from a single field. Did not find any source attributing this specific loop to one named upstream field or plant, so left blank rather than defaulting to 'Natural Gas' or guessing a basin.

Found one dollar figure repeatedly associated with Hillabee -- $240 million -- but per Williams Partners' own 10-K/10-Q disclosures this is NOT a construction cost: it's an aggregate payment Sabal Trail's member-sponsors made to Transco in three $80M installments tied to a capacity/facilities agreement (a customer payment, not Transco's capitalized cost for building the phase-1 loops). Flagging explicitly so this figure is never later mistaken for and staged as SegmentCost.
